title: Make a design's declared architecture_rules reach Fitness (.taad/fitness.yaml)
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: C1: .taad/fitness.yaml exists: missing

C2: fitness.yaml carries the five FsAnalyser rules (screen-free Core; only the classifier reads the reparse attribute, widened; directories listed only through DirectoryReader; counting-rule tests never skipped, extended; interop only in Native): missing
C3: a mechanism turns a design's declared architecture_rules into fitness.yaml, so later slices are gated: missing
C4: the Fitness gate no longer reads 'no rules declared' (Fitness op=check evaluates rules instead of NONE): missing

Does the person accept SL-022 as closing C1, C2, C4 and the effect of C3, while the mechanism half of C3 (design._append_rules in taad_v3) is verified and committed on its own? The engine's append was measured only on a working-tree copy with design.py uncommitted, and SL-020 declared four rules that never produced a file. Or should the C3 criterion be reworded, or an engine-side obligation filed?

Is any other filesystem-analyser-v2 slice in flight that has declared, or will declare, architecture_rules before SL-022 merges? Its design would append to, and so create, the same file with different content. The add/add conflict at commit-slice's refresh is one nothing resolves.

Eight split entries with exact rooted scopes (the proposal, and spike 1's 'exact scopes' option) versus five superset-scope entries (spike 1's other option, which runs .cs patterns over .csproj and .resx) versus six (spike 4's rooted translation, which splits only the interop rule). I chose eight because it is the only form that keeps each xUnit scope exact.

Two copies of the rules (yaml plus xUnit, kept in step by a header comment) versus a single source, where the test loads the yaml or a generator writes both. Rejected here as over-built for a low-risk slice, but drift has no mechanical guard.

Hand-writing the five rules versus declaring them in this design's architecture_rules so the engine's append writes them, which would exercise C3 end to end. Rejected because the record has no including_comments, so comment-only violations false-pass, and the append path is unmeasured with a non-empty list.
Naming entries as the xUnit method name plus a glob suffix, versus one plain name per rule with duplicated names across the split entries.
Leaving the mechanism half of C3 to the engine versus building a project-side converter. The over_engineering_flag pushed against the converter.

The `cases` array is still empty, for the same reason as in attempt 1. The design puts no fitness test in the .NET project. The shapes are measured by the scratch harness under %TEMP%\sl022-fitness, and its commands are listed under `tests`.

The engine-side fixes for the two remaining divergences are not built. They are `utf-8-sig` or encoding detection when opening files, and a way to read or flag files over MAX_CONTENT_BYTES, both at taad3/fitness.py:420-422. That code is in taad_v3, outside this repo and this slice. The decision on m1 says the same.

Engine (taad_v3), taad3/fitness.py:422: open covered files with encoding detection or at least `utf-8-sig`. That removes the need for `﻿?` and would let rules fire on UTF-16/UTF-32 files, where they currently match nothing.

Engine (taad_v3), taad3/fitness.py:420: a covered file over MAX_CONTENT_BYTES (2,000,000) is skipped without a word, yet its rule still counts as matched. Report it the way unmatched rules are reported, rather than letting it read as a pass.
Once the engine strips a BOM, drop `﻿?` from both patterns and from the header, so the yaml goes back to being the xUnit literal plus `(?m)`.
